ai_summary.headline: South Sudan MPCA is small (2.9% of prioritised needs) and slightly better funded than the plan, with a working CWG and JMMI.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP puts CVA at $110M, 11% of $1.04bn prioritised requirements, with MPCA only $30M (2.9%) for 475,600 people at $140 per household per month [s1]. Sectoral cash is $80M, so 73% of CVA sits with clusters. Live FTS (5 November) shows the MPC line at $33.5M and 46.9% funded ($15.7M), against 40.4% for the plan [s9]. Total CVA fell from about $197M in 2025 [s1]. The ISNA 2025 found 52% of surveyed people preferred cash to in-kind [s1]. The CWG meets monthly and runs a monthly JMMI [s5][s6], but market coverage fell from 85 to 67 markets while the MEB rose 58% in 2025 [s1]. Inference: MPCA is positioned for rapid response to new shocks but is unlikely to scale without funding, and weakening market monitoring puts transfer-value reviews at risk. CWG leadership records conflict between sources [s3][s4].
barriers: Plan only 40.4% funded; MPC line 46.9% funded ($15.7M of $33.5M) [s9]
Market monitoring coverage shrinking (85 to 67 markets) [s1]

opportunities: 52% cash preference (ISNA 2025) supports expanding MPCA beyond 27% of CVA [s1]
